patch.objective: Schedule a script with a systemd timer and service unit, catching up missed runs
secondaryObjectives: Make a scheduled job safe to rerun and to overlap with idempotent steps and a lock

sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: with Persistent=true, 'the service unit is triggered immediately if it would have been triggered at least once during the time when the timer was inactive. This is useful to catch up on missed runs of the service when the machine was off.' The page is an older systemd release; the option's meaning is unchanged in the case's terms. The case: a timer-run backup fails after a reboot; read the journal, never write into the unmounted directory, fix the mount, and rerun before the off-site copy.

Relevant text: -b, 'The argument may be empty, in which case logs for the current boot will be shown' (-1 selects the boot before); -p, 'If a single log level is specified, all messages with this log level or a lower' numeric value, that is more important, are shown; -u, 'Show messages for the specified systemd unit'; -S/--since, 'the strings "yesterday", "today", "tomorrow" are understood'; --list-boots, 'Show a tabular list of boot numbers (relative to the current boot), their IDs' and first and last message times. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14.

Relevant text: 'The previous contents (if any) and owner and mode of dir become invisible, and as long as this filesystem remains mounted, the pathname dir refers to the root of the filesystem on device.' So with nothing mounted, /mnt/backup is an ordinary directory on the root filesystem. Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. The CIFS 'mount error(13): Permission denied' line is authored in mount.cifs's style.

Relevant text: RequiresMountsFor= 'Takes a space-separated list of absolute paths. Automatically adds dependencies of type Requires= and After= for all mount units required to access the specified path.' Read through a summarizing fetch 2026-11-14. Used in the debrief as the follow-up, not as an action.
